title: Eugene Mikell, Harold Proctor and the layaway trumpet retold
summary: Carter retells how Harold Proctor and Cuban Bennett and Miley led him to a layaway trumpet bought for $33.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Yes, his name I believe, was Eugene Michael ... Lieutenant Eugene Michael, and I think he'd been
the leader of a band; you know, in World War 1.
Of course, I can't get to them without first going through the name of Harold Hal Proctor.

But I don't know if I ever mentioned that to you before, Jim. Well, Hal Proctor was the fellow that lived up the street from me. Oh, he was probably 15 or 20 years older than I me, and he played saxophone. Now after my trying to play I had... now, I had had some piano lessons from my mother and then subsequently from my older sister, and then subsequently some more lessons from the teacher who had been teaching her.
I didn't have the ... all together, this was probably about a year of piano study, after which I decided that I really didn't want to play piano; I wanted to play ...
But you did learn to read music at home.
Yes, I did learn to read music during that period, and I decided that I wanted to play a wind instrument; preferably the trumpet. I had a cousin named Cuban Bennett of whom I have spoken before.
And he played great trumpet. And Bubber Brower Miley was sort of like a neighbor; he lived around the corner -- and I admired him greatly. So I really wanted

to play the trumpet. I went and bought a trumpet, paying for it, I think, $33 -- well, not I I don't think, I know -- because I remember it very well, that it was $33, and I paid for it in 33 weeks. That was not really what we called the installment plan today; it was what we called the 'layaway' plan because you didn't get it until that last dollar had also been laid away, and until then, the instrument was laid away for you.

It happened to be that I bought this trumpet, I brought it home on a Saturday afternoon, after finishing my job with -- at the cleaners and dyes and tailors establishment where I was employed, making deliveries after school and on weekends, on Saturdays, that was.

So I got the instrument and brought it home and I thought that, 'you know, come 2 or 3 days, I'd be an instant Bubber Miley, because you know, you look up at these musicians who play and it looks so effortless, that you say, all you have to do is just pick the instrument up and put it up to your mouth, and wow! Out comes, you know, 'Wang, Wang Blues.'"
Well, it didn't exactly happen like that. And after Saturday -- come Monday, I was thoroughly discouraged with my inability to become the neighborhood virtuoso on the trumpet.
